question.text: Mr. Arvind Menon, trustee of Vindhya Event-Driven Fund (Cat III AIF), is asked whether the fund must deduct TDS under Section 194LBB of the ITA on income distributed to investors. What is the correct position?

answer.text: Yes, deduct 10% on resident and 20% on non-resident investors on all income
Yes, but only on business income
No — Section 194LBB applies only to Investment Funds referred to in Section 115UB (Category I and II). It does NOT apply to Category III
Yes, deduct at MMR 42.744% on all investors

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 194LBB is a TDS provision that operates on 'Investment Funds' whose income is passed through under Section 115UB — i.e., Category I and II AIFs. Because Category III AIFs are denied pass-through under Section 115UB, Section 194LBB is inoperative for them; tax is discharged at the fund level under trust taxation principles, not withheld on distribution. The Trap: A/B/D all assume Cat III follows Cat I/II withholding mechanics. Candidates who memorise '10%/20% TDS under 194LBB' as the AIF rule forget the scope is limited to 115UB Investment Funds. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/XIX-D drill 194LBB as the core Cat I/II TDS rule. XIX-E reverses it — the ABSENCE of 194LBB is the Cat III fingerprint. XIX-B (Cat III Distributor) also tests the no-TDS angle for investor communications. Manager's Pro-Tip: At Vindhya, since there is no 194LBB deduction on distribution, the fund itself pays fund-level tax and distributes post-tax. Make sure the LP agreement and Form 64D statements reflect this — any LP expecting a 194LBB credit in Form 26AS will be unpleasantly surprised.
